How to estimate future car resale value

Start with a current private-party value supported by comparable vehicles or a recognized valuation service. Enter how long you plan to keep the car and an annual depreciation assumption. The calculator projects market value, estimated selling costs, loan payoff at sale, and net proceeds.

projected resale value = current value x (1 - annual depreciation rate)^years

estimated net proceeds = resale value - selling costs - future loan payoff

Car resale example

A car worth $28,000 today, depreciating 14% annually for three years, has a projected resale value of $17,809.57. With 2% selling costs and an $8,000 payoff at sale, estimated net proceeds are $9,453.38.

Slower and faster depreciation scenarios

The scenario range changes only the annual depreciation rate. With a 14% entered rate and a 3-point range, the table compares 11%, 14%, and 17%. It holds the starting value, holding period, payoff, selling-cost percentage, and mileage constant so you can see how sensitive the result is to the rate assumption.

Current value is the critical input

Use a local value for the same year, make, model, trim, drivetrain, mileage, and condition. Consumer Reports vehicle-value guidance notes that condition, high mileage, damage, and reconditioning needs affect value. Edmunds appraisal guidance also describes local market and vehicle-specific factors. This calculator does not have live VIN, auction, or listing data.

Loan payoff and selling costs

Enter the expected lender payoff at the future sale date, not today's payoff and not the sum of scheduled payments. Selling costs are modeled as a percentage of projected value and can represent listing, inspection, detailing, transaction, or consignment costs. Set the percentage to zero when those costs do not apply.

Resale value versus depreciation

This page focuses on future cash proceeds. Use the car depreciation calculator to compare constant and two-stage value loss with a residual floor and cost per mile. Use the used car value calculator for current retail, private-party, and trade-in ranges from local comparable data.

Frequently asked questions

Is the projected resale value guaranteed?

No. It is a scenario based on your current value and entered rate. Obtain current appraisals when you are ready to sell.

What if net proceeds are negative?

A negative result means the modeled payoff and selling costs exceed the projected sale value. That indicates possible negative equity under the assumptions.

Does annual mileage reduce the resale value automatically?

No. It reports projected total mileage and depreciation per mile. Reflect an expected mileage penalty in the current value or annual depreciation assumption.
